page: Microsoft Azure D8ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, providing 472 GB of local disk capacity with Premium Storage capability. The hypervisor layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top 25% placement in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores. Text processing is a notable strength, ranking in the top 10% of Geekbench benchmarks. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth presents a clear tradeoff: while small-block cached read-only bandwidth is average at 607.6 GB/sec, large-block uncached read-only bandwidth drops to the bottom 25% at 38.94 GB/sec.

This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources and local storage without the premium of memory-optimized instances. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, text processing, software compilation, and database operations. However, the weak uncached memory bandwidth and lower performance on medium-sized LLM prompt processing suggest it is less optimal for memory-intensive data science or large-scale AI inference.
